messages.content: Predict the participant's recorded financial decision in an online study with an effort task and a money-allocation task. Their order is counterbalanced; this prediction input does not identify which came first or provide experience from the other task. The beneficiary described as OTHER is an entirely anonymous unknown future participant; no name, age, gender, photograph or biography of that person is provided. Participants are told the study is newly launched and designated money for others will go to future participants. Use the information presented to the decision-maker. Dollar amounts are money; probabilities are separate chances of reward, not amounts or proportions donated. A12% chance means12 in100,50% means half, and88% means88 in100, without guaranteeing a win. The fixed $7 participation fee is separate from task-dependent bonuses. Participants are given an estimated task duration without being told the exact total trial count. The current decision occurs before this trial's work, lottery outcome or final bonus selection. Own demographic responses were collected before the tasks. Earlier same-task records, when supplied, occurred before the current decision. Other-task experience, exact task order and unprovided past events are unavailable to this prediction input; missing input does not mean the participant did not experience or remember them. Do not invent unavailable information or give a normative answer. Choose between EASY and HARD before performing the current physical task. EASY requires30spacebar presses within7seconds and offers a possible $1.00. HARD requires100key presses within20seconds: first50with the left arrow and then50with the right arrow. These demands are fixed across people, not calibrated to personal ability. After EASY there is a10second delay before the next trial. The HARD reward is the currently displayed amount supplied in user. Both options have the same displayed chance of winning, conditional on completing the chosen task successfully within its time limit. Failure earns no trial reward; success can still yield no money if the lottery loses. For SELF, all of this trial's reward is for the decision-maker; for OTHER, all is designated for an anonymous future participant and none for the decision-maker. This is a choice of work/reward option, not splitting money. Participants are told one self-benefit trial and one other-benefit trial will be randomly selected for bonus allocation at the end. After a choice, the person performs the task and sees completion/reward feedback. Earlier records in user report the choice and completed/won flags (true=yes,false=no); reward_dollars is the money won on that earlier trial for its beneficiary, not a guaranteed payment across every trial. Earlier exact key-press counts are not supplied. The target is the initial EASY/HARD choice regardless of subsequent completion or win. Reply with exactly EASY or HARD, no explanation.
